cases.statement: Three people: the index patient (59-year-old Spanish man, homozygous, whole-exome sequencing); a living sibling said to carry 'the same variants in homozygous state' (no testing details); and a patient previously reported by Fasano et al. (ref 38), compound heterozygous, cited only in the Discussion with no case description or second allele.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: HDL-C 2 mg/dL and ApoA-I 0 mg/dL; orange-colored tonsils; massive hepatosplenomegaly; foamy histiocytes in liver and bone marrow; mild low platelet count

quotes.quote: A recently retired 59-year-old Spanish male with sedentary lifestyle and current smoking habit was referred to our institution because of unexplained hepatosplenomegaly.
The NGS analysis allowed the identification of a homozygous missense variant, c.4799A>G (p. His1600Arg) in ABCA1 gene (NM_005502.4).
high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C): 2 mg/dL (NR: 34–91)
apolipoprotein A (ApoA-I): 0 mg/dL
orange-colored tonsils (Figure 1—left)
distended abdomen with massive hepatosplenomegaly (Figure 1—middle)
Liver biopsy showed aggregates of histiocytes with foamy PAS-negative cytoplasm, diffusely distributed throughout the lobule, portal spaces, and centrilobular region (Figure 2—right).
Further laboratory investigations of blood evidenced mild low red cell and platelet counts

people.label: sibling of patient
people.zygosity_or_genotype: homozygous (as stated: 'the same variants in homozygous state')
people.key_phenotypes: low HDL-C (described only as 'a similar clinical presentation')

quotes.quote: the fifth one is still alive, diagnosed with the same variants in homozygous state and with a similar clinical presentation of low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C).

Fasano et al. [38] reported a patient who was compound heterozygous for a nucleotide substitution of c.4799A>G (p. His1600Arg) which was considered probably damaging based on predictive in silico analysis.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Person-level (index patient): features the authors call typical of TD (undetectable HDL-C and ApoA-I, orange tonsils, hepatosplenomegaly, foamy histiocytes, thrombocytopenia); diagnosis by the Koseki criteria; secondary causes of dyslipidemia ruled out. WES was performed, but the paper does not report whether other genes (e.g. LCAT, APOA1) carried variants. The patient also had MGUS, which the panel may weigh as a possible contributor to hepatosplenomegaly or cytopenias (not discussed as such by the authors).

quotes.quote: we describe a case study of a 59-year-old male patient with features typical of TD
Secondary causes of hyperlipidemia were ruled out and we focused on assessing for rare hereditary metabolic disorders of lipid metabolism.
The definitive diagnosis of Tangier disease was made considering the Koseki criteria [24].
Patient’s DNA was isolated from 400 μL of blood collected in EDTA following standard procedures and whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed.
At that time, there was history of monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) involving IgG kappa and IgA lambda monoclonal cell populations not showing disease progression.

segregation.statement: One living sibling is reported homozygous with low HDL-C (testing details not given). Three brothers died of premature cardiovascular disease with neuropathy, low ApoA-I, thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly but were never genetically tested. Parents died at an elderly age; their genotypes are not reported.

quotes.quote: the fifth one is still alive, diagnosed with the same variants in homozygous state and with a similar clinical presentation of low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C).
the patient’s parents both died at an elderly age, and three brothers had died as a result of premature cardiovascular death.
it seems reasonable to conclude those three siblings with unexpected sudden death could be also affected by TD, although this cannot be confirmed due to the lack of genetic testing.

in_trans.statement: Index patient and sibling reported homozygous; parents not tested (deceased); consanguinity not reported. The ref [38] patient is compound heterozygous, but the second allele and phase are not given in this paper.

Fasano et al. [38] reported a patient who was compound heterozygous for a nucleotide substitution of c.4799A>G (p. His1600Arg) which was considered probably damaging based on predictive in silico analysis.

functional.statement: No laboratory functional assay. The only 'functional' evidence is a SWISS-MODEL homology model (computational; see computational_predictions).

quotes.quote: This homology model was used in order to investigate how the homozygous variant detected in our patient could alter the protein structure, potentially resulting in conformational changes with a significant impact on function (most likely loss of function).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense, p.(His1600Arg), per the batch HGVS (matches the paper). The authors place His1600 in the extracellular domain ECD2 and propose loss of function.

quotes.quote: ABCA1 mediates the delivery of phospholipids and cholesterol from the membrane to ApoA-I and p.His1600Arg is precisely located on the ECD2 domain which is responsible for binding to ApoA-II [49].
potentially resulting in conformational changes with a significant impact on function (most likely loss of function)

computational_predictions.statement: MutationTaster: disease-causing; DANN 0.9984 ('damaging'); GERP, PhyloP and phastCons: highly conserved region; SWISS-MODEL predicts structural changes in ECD1/ECD2. Fasano et al. reportedly predicted it 'probably damaging' in silico (tool not named here). Table S1 with full in-silico results is not in the text available.

quotes.quote: Pathogenicity was predicted using MutationTaster (disease-causing) and by calculating the DANN score (score: 0.9984) which corresponded to “damaging”.
According to GERP, PhyloP, and phastCons, the variant c.4799A>G is placed in a highly conserved region of the ABCA1 protein.

The protein modelling of wild-type and mutated ABCA1 showed predicted changes in spatial protein structure (Figure 3B) affecting the structural conformation of ECD1 and ECD2 in the extracellular region.

Fasano et al. [38] reported a patient who was compound heterozygous for a nucleotide substitution of c.4799A>G (p. His1600Arg) which was considered probably damaging based on predictive in silico analysis.

population_data_in_papers.statement: The authors state the variant was not referenced in population databases such as gnomAD (exome and genome).

quotes.quote: It was not cited on ClinVar, nor was it referenced in population databases such as GnomAD (exome and genome) or correlated with patient’s phenotype

authors_classification.statement: Authors classify it as likely pathogenic with ACMG criteria PM2, PM5, PP3 and PP4 (authors' own statement). Fasano et al. (as cited) considered it probably damaging in silico.

quotes.quote: classified as “likely pathogenic” according to the following ACMG criteria: PM2, PM5, PP3, and PP4 [25].

Fasano et al. [38] reported a patient who was compound heterozygous for a nucleotide substitution of c.4799A>G (p. His1600Arg) which was considered probably damaging based on predictive in silico analysis.

concerns: The paper's title calls the variant 'novel', but the Discussion cites Fasano et al. [38] reporting the same variant (compound heterozygous); the claim is 'identified for the first time as homozygous'.

TANGIER-ID0229 is a secondary citation of Fasano et al. 2012 (reference list PMID 22959828) with no case description or second allele here; if that paper is in the corpus, the same person may also appear there under another identity.
Sibling (TANGIER-ID0060): 'diagnosed with the same variants in homozygous state' uses the plural 'variants'; no testing method, sex or detailed phenotype is given.
One of the ACMG criteria the authors cite (see authors_classification) concerns a different missense change at the same residue; no such other change at His1600 is described in the paper.
Index patient also has MGUS; three brothers' neuropathy was diagnosed as probable leprosy (authors suggest misdiagnosis).
Section heading '3.2. AGK Protein Modeling' names a different gene (AGK) although the text models ABCA1; likely an editorial error.
Variant calls were made on GRCh37/hg19; transcript NM_005502.4 matches the batch.
Supplementary Table S1 (in-silico details) and S2 are not in the text read here.
notes_for_panel: Homozygous index patient with classic TD features and a reportedly homozygous sibling with low HDL; three untested deceased brothers with suggestive features. Evidence for function is in silico only. The authors' own classification and criteria are quoted under authors_classification. A prior compound-heterozygous patient is cited from Fasano et al. 2012.
